Popular singer, Peter Okoye, popularly known as Mr P, has reaffirmed his confidence in his musical abilities, saying his latest album, OG Forever, reflects his ambition to make a lasting contribution to Afrobeats. He spoke at an exclusive listening party for the 15-track album held at Proxy Lagos on Wednesday, November 18, two days before its official release on November 20. Mr P sparked conversations on social media in January when he declared his intention to make one of the best albums in the history of Afrobeats. The statement attracted criticism from some music fans, particularly on X, formerly Twitter , with some questioning his confidence. At the listening session, the singer stood by his declaration, expressing confidence in the quality of the project and his determination to create music that would stand the test of time. The event also provided an opportunity for him to discuss the personal experiences, creative decisions and influences that shaped the album. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources One of the songs that particularly challenged him was Wish You Well, which he identified as one of the most difficult tracks to create, both artistically and emotionally. The singer also spoke about his relationship with Ghanaian music lovers, acknowledging their support and explaining how it influenced his decision to feature Ghanaian dancehall star, Stonebwoy, on the album. The collaboration, titled No Case, also features Tanzanian singer, Juma Jux. Mr P praised Stonebwoy’s energy, musical style and distinctive personality, saying he admired the confidence with which the artiste carried himself. He added that the collaboration was also a way of appreciating his Ghanaian audience for their consistent support. Smart devices redefining music entertainment Big Oly takes Afrobeats yacht parties to Los Angeles Young Jonn, Desperados promote carefree living with ‘Let It Go’ The growing influence of artificial intelligence on music production was another subject discussed at the event. Mr P shared his views on the use of AI in the creative process, stressing the importance of human direction in making the technology useful to artistes. He cited Back to Back while discussing AI-assisted mixing, giving guests an insight into how emerging technology is being incorporated into contemporary music production. Known for combining music with choreography and elaborate visual storytelling, the singer also discussed the creative direction behind I Can’t Look Away. He revealed that he personally handled the costumes for 85 dancers featured in the song’s music video, underscoring the attention given to choreography, costumes and performance in translating his musical ideas into visual productions. Hosted by broadcaster Do2dtun, the event allowed guests to listen to the album and interact with the singer about his creative journey. It attracted several entertainment personalities, including actors Toyin Abraham, Damilola Adegbite and Beverly Osu; singers 2Baba, Spyro and Ric Hassani; reality TV star Alex Asogwa, popularly known as Alex Unusual; comedian Cute Abiola; and social media personality Purple Speedy, among others. One of the highlights came during the after-party when Toyin Abraham joined Mr P on the drums as he performed I Can’t Look Away, drawing cheers from guests. The 15-track OG Forever marks another phase in the singer’s solo career, bringing together collaborations, musical experimentation and his continued interest in dance-driven performances.
